partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to protein S deficiency, autosomal dominant
partners.mechanism_chain: F9 (HGNC:3790) —DISRUPTS→ coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VIVO-113705); coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VIVO-113705) —LEADS_TO→ bleeding (HP:0001892); PROS1 (HGNC:9658) —DISRUPTS→ coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VIVO-113705); coagulation cascade (REACT:R-VIVO-113705) —LEADS_TO→ thrombophilia (HP:0002685). Loss-of-function mutations in F9 impair the intrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade, leading to bleeding diathesis (hemophilia B). Conversely, loss-of-function mutations in PROS1 impair the protein S-mediated inhibition of factors Va and VIIIa, disrupting the balance of the coagulation cascade and leading to a hypercoagulable state (thrombophilia). Both diseases thus converge on the central coagulation cascade, but with opposing functional outcomes.
